title: BE012O1R field packet
subtitle: Rifle - Trappers Lake - optional Chapman
stance: Legality first. The mapped rule screen, current ownership, posted closures, and a safe backstop are go/no-go items. The 0.25- and 0.5-mile rings are optional planning context, not legal setbacks.

hunt.legalHours: One-half hour before sunrise through one-half hour after sunset. Use the CPW/NOAA time for the exact location.

itinerary.title: Rifle charge, zero, then settle in
itinerary.plan: Charge at Rifle, drive to West Rifle Creek SWA, use the designated range before sunset, occupy the signed SWA campground, and scout a Rifle corridor if daylight remains.
itinerary.sleep: West Rifle Creek SWA campground - night 1 of 2
itinerary.decision: The range is closed sunset to sunrise. Camping is lawful here for a licensed hunter during this active big-game season.

itinerary.title: Full Rifle hunt day
itinerary.plan: Hunt the Rifle cluster at first and last light. Start with H01B for the strongest all-federal map signal; use H01D as the shorter secondary scout.
itinerary.sleep: West Rifle Creek SWA campground - night 2 of 2
itinerary.decision: Do not treat Rifle Falls State Park or a developed campground as a shooting area. Confirm the occupied point is on huntable land.

itinerary.title: Top off in Rifle, loop through Meeker
itinerary.plan: Return to the Rifle Supercharger and leave near the charge level selected in the car for the remote loop. Take CO 13 to Meeker, then CR 8 and FR 205 to Trappers Lake. Scout or hunt H02A or H02D.
itinerary.sleep: Shepherds Rim if signed open/available; otherwise a posted-legal established dispersed site below the lake complex
itinerary.decision: Horse Thief is stock-users-only. Trappers Lake wilderness camping exclusions still apply even when a pullout looks established.

itinerary.title: Dawn at Trappers; Chapman is optional
itinerary.plan: Hunt Trappers at first light. Add Chapman only if time, charge, and the signed road status support it; otherwise exit toward the Kremmling Supercharger. At Chapman, start with H03C or H03A.
itinerary.sleep: Return Tuesday; if extending, use the signed Chapman campground or a legal FR 940 dispersed site
itinerary.decision: The Tesla decides road suitability in the field. The packet does not impose a weather-based closure that the land manager has not imposed.

legalRules.label: LICENSE / PLACE
legalRules.rule: Carry the valid BE012O1R license and hunt only its listed GMUs. A hunting license satisfies West Rifle Creek SWA access during the season.
legalRules.fieldAction: Keep the license and photo ID on you; keep the offline GMU/ownership layers available.

legalRules.label: HOURS / ORANGE
legalRules.rule: Legal big-game hours are one-half hour before sunrise through one-half hour after sunset. A firearm bear hunter needs 500 square inches of solid fluorescent orange or pink above the waist plus a visible-from-all-directions hat.
legalRules.fieldAction: Set daily alarms from the exact-location sunrise/sunset and wear compliant solid color.

legalRules.label: SHOT LOCATION
legalRules.rule: On National Forest land, do not discharge within 150 yards of a residence, building, campsite, developed recreation site, or occupied area, or across/in a manner exposing a person or property. Colorado also prohibits firing from, on, or across a public road; firearm/bow shooters must be at least 50 feet from the road centerline.
legalRules.fieldAction: Use the red rule screen as the initial map filter, then confirm the real facility edge, road, ownership, target, and backstop on site.

legalRules.label: BAIT
legalRules.rule: It is illegal to hunt big game over bait regardless of who placed it. Food, refuse, animal parts, salt, minerals, grain, and food-scent products cannot be put out as an attraction.
legalRules.fieldAction: Store camp food; never place or expose it to influence bear movement, and do not make the camp/vehicle the shot focus.

legalRules.label: FOOD STORAGE
legalRules.rule: On White River National Forest from May 15 through October 1, unattended attractants must use an allowed method. A closed, locked hard-sided vehicle is expressly allowed; so is an IGBC-certified bear-resistant container. The cited order does not prescribe a tent-to-vehicle distance.
legalRules.fieldAction: Put food, trash, toiletries, cooking residue, and scented gear in the locked Tesla with all openings closed, or use an approved locker/canister.

legalRules.label: DEFENSE OF PROPERTY
legalRules.rule: Colorado allows wildlife to be killed only when necessary to prevent death, damage, or injury to human life, livestock, real property, or a motor vehicle. Any wildlife killed remains state property and must be reported to CPW within five days.
legalRules.fieldAction: A bear merely approaching or investigating is not automatically the necessity finding. Avoid, deter, document, and call CPW; use force only when the statutory necessity actually exists.

legalRules.label: AFTER A KILL
legalRules.rule: Immediately sign, date, detach, and attach the carcass tag. Leave evidence of sex naturally attached; recover the edible meat. Personally present the unfrozen head and hide to CPW within five working days for report, seal, and tooth extraction.
legalRules.fieldAction: Mark the kill GPS coordinate and GMU, preserve the head/hide unfrozen, and call the nearest CPW office during business hours.

camps.name: West Rifle Creek SWA campground
camps.location: Campground on CR 252, four miles northwest of Hwy 325; follow CPW signs
camps.legal: Camping is limited to licensed hunters during an established big-game season and the three days before/after. Fires only in a containment structure.
camps.food: Use the locked Tesla for attractants when unattended; leave the tent free of food and cooking residue.
camps.note: This is the range/camp stop. It is not Rifle Falls State Park.

camps.name: Shepherds Rim Campground
camps.legal: Use only a signed open and available site. The listing provides bear lockers at each site.
camps.food: Use the provided locker or the locked vehicle whenever attractants are unattended.
camps.note: The campground overlaps the modeled food-source footprint, but that is a hunting-quality issue, not a camping prohibition.

camps.name: Lower FR 205 / CR 8 dispersed
camps.fit: TRAPPERS PREFERRED BASE IF LEGAL ON SITE
camps.location: Use a previously occupied pullout below the developed complex only after checking the current MVUM, signs, and land ownership
camps.legal: Inside Flat Tops Wilderness, camping is prohibited within 100 feet of water, a system trail, or restoration/no-camping signs, and within one-quarter mile of Trappers Lake. Vehicle camping must also stay on an open motor route.
camps.food: Locked hard-sided vehicle is an allowed White River food-storage method through October 1.
camps.note: Previously disturbed ground is evidence of use, not by itself legal authority.

camps.name: Horse Thief Campground
camps.legal: All seven sites are set aside for stock users only.
camps.food: Bear boxes are provided, but that does not change site eligibility.
camps.note: Do not use for this non-stock trip.

camps.name: Chapman Reservoir / FR 940
camps.legal: The developed campground is the clean legal fallback when signed open. Dispersed sites require an open motor route, public land, and no posted closure.
camps.food: Use the locked vehicle or any provided approved storage for all unattended attractants.
camps.note: The official facility description calls the main approach gravel 2WD; the final occupied site still controls.

charging.name: Rifle Supercharger
charging.detail: 12 stalls, up to 250 kW, 24/7. Use before West Rifle and again before the Meeker/Trappers loop.

charging.name: Kremmling Supercharger
charging.detail: 8 stalls, up to 250 kW, 24/7. Use as the eastern exit checkpoint.

scoutCards.camp: Shepherds Rim or legal lower-road dispersed site
Chapman campground or verified FR 940 dispersed site

goNoGo: GO: valid unit and season; public/huntable parcel; no closure; outside the actual discharge exclusion; safe target and backstop; legal road position; legal hours.
NO-GO: private/unknown land without permission; posted closure; developed/occupied-area discharge zone; road violation; bait relationship; cub/family group; unsafe backstop.
FIELD JUDGMENT: clearance, mud, rut depth, center crown, weather, fire choice, optional caution-ring separation, and whether current sign justifies spending time.
checklist: License, photo ID, hunter education proof if required, carcass tag intact
Solid fluorescent orange/pink outer garment and visible hat
Offline Hunting Atlas/ownership, Hunt Assist GPX, MVUMs, paper field packet
Rifle, legal ammunition, case, eye/ear protection, zeroing targets
Binoculars (do not identify bears through a rifle scope), rangefinder, headlamp
Tent/sleep system; food and every scented item consolidated for locked-car storage
Game bags, gloves, knife, cooling plan, cord, evidence-of-sex plan
Phone power, charging adapters/cables, tire kit, compressor, recovery/traction basics
Exact cash/check for remote fee sites, water, and a no-fire cooking option
